कुबे(वे)रः [कुत्सितं बे(वे)रं शरीरं यस्य सः]
—1 The god of riches and treasure and the regent of the northern quarter;
 कुबेरगुप्तां दिशमुष्णरश्मौ गन्तुं प्रवृत्ते समयं विलङ्घ्य Ku. 3. 25
 (vide Malli. thereon). [Kubera is the son of Viśravas by Iḍāviḍā,
 and thus the half brother of Rāvaṇa. Besides, being the lord of riches
 and regent of the north, he is the king of the Yakṣas and Kinnaras, and
 a friend of Rudra. His abode is Kailāsa. He is represented as being deformed
 in body-having three legs, only eight teeth, and a yellow mark in place of one eye.]
—2 N. of a tree.
.━{@Comp.@}: कुबेराक्षी, कुबेराद्रिः, कुबेराचलः, कुबेरदिश्, कुबेरबान्धवः

कुबेरः + -अद्रिः, -अचलः an epithet of mountain Kailāsa.

कुब्ज a. [कु ईषत् उब्जमार्जवं यत्र शकं˚ Tv.] Hump-backed,
 crooked. अन्धाः खञ्जाः कुब्जा वामनकाश्च Garbha. Up. 3.

कुब्ज + .{@-ब्जा@} A young female servant of Kaṃsa, said to be deformed in
 three parts of her body. [Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, while proceeding to
 Mathurā, saw her on the high road carrying unguent to Kaṃsa. They asked
 her if she would give them some portion of it, and she gave as much as
 they wanted. Kṛṣṇa, being very much pleased with her kindness, made
 her perfectly straight, and she began to appear a most beautiful woman.]
.━{@Comp.@}: कुब्जकिरातः, कुब्जवामनः, कुब्जगामिन्, कुब्जलीला
